tools.name: studio_status
tools.title: Get the status of the studio
tools.description: Gives the state of the agent server: the profile, the active mod, the revision, the undo and redo steps, the tool groups and the limits. This tool changes nothing. Call it first.

host.description: editor for the agent server of the editor, headless for oltool mcp serve.

profile.description: The name of the open profile, or none while no profile is open.

mods.description: The ids of the mods of the profile, in load order.

active_mod.description: The id of the mod that gets the edits, or none.

tier.description: The tier of the active mod: 1 for data only, 2 for the OpenLancer runtime.

targets.description: The ids of the target games of the active mod, for example vanilla-1.1.

can_edit.description: True when the host takes edits now. When it is false, reason tells why.

reason.description: Why the host takes no edits now, or none.

dirty.description: True when the session has edits that it did not save.

rev.description: The revision of the edit view, as text. Each edit, undo and redo increases it. A save does not change it.

label.description: The label of the step.

origin.description: Who made the step: user, agent or recovery.

undo.description: The step that Undo reverses, or none.

label.description: The label of the step.

origin.description: Who made the step: user, agent or recovery.

redo.description: The step that Redo does again, or none.

system.description: The system: reference of the system that the Scene shows, or none.

mission.description: The msn: reference of the mission script that the editor shows, or none.

cutscene.description: The thn: reference of the cutscene that the editor shows, or none.

view.description: What the editor shows now, or none in the host without a window.

paused.description: True while the user pauses the edits of the agent.

tool_groups.description: The tool groups that the user shows. A tool of another group gives not_available.

list_rows.description: The rows of a page when the call gives no limit.

max_list_rows.description: The largest limit of one page.

result_kilobytes.description: The most text of one result, in KB. A larger result gives the error limit.

calls_per_second.description: The most calls that the server takes in one second.

wait_seconds.description: How long a call waits while the user edits, in seconds. Then it gives busy.

tail_seconds.description: How long the second part of a call can run, for example a target check, in seconds.

render_pixels.description: The most pixels on each side of an image of render_scene and render_cutscene. A larger panel of capture_panel gives a smaller image.

edit_items.description: The most items that one call of delete_items or duplicate_items names, and the most rows of scene_transform and cutscene_move_events.

edit_sections.description: The most sections that one edit call changes, adds or removes.

batch_steps.description: The most steps of one edit_batch call, and the most commands of one mission_edit call. A command_group counts as one command.

route_legs.description: The most legs of one route of scene_place_patrol_route.

export_minutes.description: How long one export can take, in minutes.

code.description: The kind of the error. Each kind has a fixed meaning, for example not_found or invalid_argument.

detail.description: The detail code of the error, for example ReferenceNotFound or BadArgument.

message.description: What is wrong and how to correct it.

index.description: The index of the step of a batch that failed, or none.

target.description: The reference or the text that the error is about, or none.

field.description: The argument or the field that the error is about, or none.

step_code.description: For the error step_failed: the code of the error of the step, for example not_found. Else none.

anyOf.description: A result of the tool. The structured content of a call is a result or a tool error.
A tool error. The call has isError true. Read the message, then correct the call.

mod.description: The id of the mod of the layer lower_mod or active_mod, else none.

origin.description: The layer of the edit view that gives the item, and if the item has an edit that is not saved.

total.description: The number of rows of all pages.

next_cursor.description: The cursor of the next page, or none on the last page. Give it as the argument cursor.

detail.description: The detail code of the error, for example ReferenceNotFound or BadArgument.

message.description: What is wrong and how to correct it.

index.description: The index of the step of a batch that failed, or none.

target.description: The reference or the text that the error is about, or none.

field.description: The argument or the field that the error is about, or none.

step_code.description: For the error step_failed: the code of the error of the step, for example not_found. Else none.

anyOf.description: A result of the tool. The structured content of a call is a result or a tool error.
A tool error. The call has isError true. Read the message, then correct the call.

detail.description: The detail code of the error, for example ReferenceNotFound or BadArgument.

tools.name: mission_dry_run
tools.title: Dry run a mission
tools.description: Runs the trigger rules of the retail game on one mission script, step by step, without a game world. You give the inputs. An input starts the mission, loads a checkpoint, starts at a trigger, runs an active trigger or says that an event happens. It can also set a fact or the place of the player, or advance the time in heartbeats of 1/30 s. The result gives each step with its changes in the order of the game, and the state after the last step. The query keeps no state, so send all inputs at each call. This tool changes nothing.

script.description: The reference of a mission script, for example msn:DATA\MISSIONS\M01A\m01a.ini.

inputs.description: The inputs in order, at most 1000, with at most 108000 heartbeats in all. Each input is an object with a kind. The kinds are start_mission, load_checkpoint {trigger}, start_at {trigger}, run_trigger {trigger}, event {line} and fact {line, on}. The other kinds are heartbeats {count} or {until_timer: true}, player_system {system} and player_in_space {value}. A trigger is a trg: reference or the nickname of a trigger of the script. A line is {key, values} with the value names of describe_mission_name. A value that the line does not give matches any value. When it matches two waiting lines, the line whose values it gives in full is the event. Else the call gives invalid_argument. start_mission, load_checkpoint and start_at start a new run and remove the inputs before them. start_at starts the triggers that wait at a trigger, as a play from that trigger does. The fact and player inputs before them stay, in their net form.

timer_bound.description: Which bound of a timer range the run uses. The game picks a value in the range when the mission loads.

since_step.description: Give only the steps after this step. The state after the last step always comes. Use it as the page of a long run.

script.description: The msn: reference of the script.

version.description: The version of the script that the run read. It changes at each change of the script.

total_steps.description: The number of all steps of the run: one step for each input that the run keeps.

step.description: The number of the step, from 1. Each input that the run keeps gives one step.

cause.description: The input of the step in plain words, for example Start mission or Comm line X ends.

heartbeats.description: The heartbeats since the start of the run at the end of the step.

steps.description: The steps after since_step, in order.

active.description: The trg: references of the active triggers, in the order of the active list.

pending.description: The trg: references of the triggers that start at the next event or heartbeat, smallest game id first.

errors.description: The errors of a refusal. A tool error gives them as the error of the call.

undo_label.description: The label of the Undo step, for example Agent: Delete my_station_1, or none without a step.

rev.description: The revision of the edit view after the call, as text. A preview and a call without a change keep it.

versions.description: The versions of the mission scripts that the edit changed, by install path.

files.description: The install paths of the files that the edit changed.

adds.description: The references of the new items.

changes.description: The references of the items that the edit changed and kept.

ref.description: The reference of the removed item.

why.description: target for an item of the request, cascade for an item that goes with a target.

cause.description: For a cascade: the line that names the target. Else none.

deletes.description: The items that the edit removed.

renames.description: The items that got a new name, with the old and the new reference.

key.description: The key of the first line.

fixes.description: The lines that the edit changed because they name an item that the edit removed.

key.description: The key of the line.

consequence.description: What the game does with the line.

blocks_save.description: True when the line stops the save until a fix.

missing.description: The lines that show 'Missing' after the edit.

new_problems.description: The problems of the checks that the edit adds. The edit applied.

fixed_problems.description: The problems of the checks that the edit removes.

needs_confirmation.description: True when the edit changes more than its targets. The real call then needs confirm: true.

select.description: The item that the editor selects after the edit, or none.

patch.description: With with_patch: the patch text of each changed INI file and cutscene, by install path.

field.description: The argument or the field that the error is about, or none.

tools.name: mission_edit
tools.title: Run mission commands
tools.description: Runs mission commands as one Undo step, all or nothing. Each command sees the result of the commands before it. The tool refuses an edit that adds an error to a script. The result gives the inverse: give it to this tool to revert the edit after later edits. Read get_mission and describe_mission_name first. Set preview to true to see the result first.

label.description: The label of the Undo step. Without it, the edit takes the label of its one command, or 'Mission edit'.

commands.description: The mission commands in order. Each command is an object with a kind, for example add_trigger. A line is {key, values} with the value names of describe_mission_name. studio_status gives the most commands of one call. One call runs at most 1000 mission commands, also each command in a command_group.

options.description: reject_new_errors is always true: an edit that adds an error changes nothing. Set reject_new_warnings to true to also refuse an edit that adds a warning. Then a new warning gives new_errors with the detail NewWarnings.

expect_versions.description: The versions of the scripts that you read, by install path. When a script has another version now, the edit gives stale_revision.

preview.description: Show what the edit does, and change nothing. The revision stays the same.

if_revision.description: Refuse the edit when the edit view changed after this revision. Give the rev of a result that you read.

with_patch.description: With preview: also give the patch text of each INI file and each cutscene that the edit changes.

confirm.description: Apply an edit that changes more than its targets. Without it, such an edit gives needs_confirmation.

section.description: The sec: reference of the section, or the trg: reference of a trigger.

hash.description: The hash of the base section to write: 16 hex digits. Without it, the command writes the hash of the base data now.

accept_base.description: Accepts the base data now for a section of the active mod, after the base data changed. The lines of the section do not change.

script.description: The msn: reference of the mission script.

nickname.description: The nickname of the new act. Without it, the editor makes the nickname act_<n>.

name.description: The name of the act that the editor shows. Without it, the name is 'Act <n>'.

text.description: The walkthrough text of the act.

members.description: The nicknames of the triggers of the act, in order.

index.description: The place of the act in the list of the acts, from 0. Without it, the act goes to the end.

add_act.description: Adds an act to the graph file of the script. The game does not read the acts. A trigger is in one act, so each member leaves its other act.

trigger.description: The trg: reference of the trigger.

line.description: The action, for example {"key": "Act_ActTrig", "values": {"trigger": "my_next"}}.

before.description: The row of the trigger that the action goes before, from 0. Without it, the action goes to the end.

add_action.description: Adds an action line to a trigger, before a row or at the end. An action cannot go before the nickname line or the condition.

script.description: The msn: reference of the mission script.

item_kind.description: The kind of the item, for example formation or ship_build. A section type, for example MsnFormation, is also correct.

nickname.description: The nickname of the new item. Without it, the editor makes a free name.

lines.description: The lines of the new item, each with its key and its values by name.

add_item.description: Adds an item to a mission script. The item kinds are formation, solar, loot, order_list, objective, conversation, npc, random_encounter and ship_build. A ship build goes into the ship build file of the script.

item.description: The sec: reference of the item.

label.description: The label, for example my_wing. A condition or an action can name all items with the label.

add_label.description: Adds a label line to a ship, a formation, a solar or a loot. The line goes before the first formation or ship line.

script.description: The msn: reference of the mission script.

nickname.description: The nickname of the new ship. Without it, the editor makes a free name.

npc.description: The nickname of an existing [NPC] of the script. Without it, the command adds a new [NPC] with the pilot.

faction.description: The faction of the pilot, for example my_faction.

head.description: The head of the pilot in the comm window.

body.description: The body of the pilot in the comm window.

accessories.description: The accessories of the pilot in the comm window.

name_text.description: The text id of the name of the pilot: a number, or $str:<key>.

pilot.description: The pilot of a new [NPC]: its faction, its voice, its look and its name.

build.description: The nickname of an existing ship build. Without it, the command adds the ship build of new_build.

archetype.description: The ship archetype of the build, for example my_ship.

loadout.description: The loadout of the build, for example my_loadout.

pilot.description: The pilot of the build, for example my_pilot.

state_graph.description: The state graph: FIGHTER, TRANSPORT, GUNBOAT, CRUISER, NOTHING or PLAYER.

level.description: The level of the build, for example d5.

npc_classes.description: The NPC classes of the build.

new_build.description: A new ship build: its ship archetype, its loadout and its other lines. It goes into the ship build file of the script.

position.description: The start position: three numbers x, y and z.

rotation.description: The start orientation: four numbers, as an orientation line holds them.

anchor.description: The nickname of the object, for example my_station.

heading.description: The heading from the object, in degrees.

range.description: The range from the object, in meters. It is optional.

near.description: A place near an object, in place of the position. The command writes a rel_pos line.

system.description: The nickname of the system of the ship, for example my_system.

labels.description: The labels of the ship, for example my_wing.

orders.description: The nickname of the order list that the ship starts with.

add_mission_ship.description: Adds a mission ship as one step. The command adds an [MsnShip] at the end of the script, a new [NPC] and a new ship build. An existing [NPC] or ship build can take the place of a new one.

order_list.description: The sec: reference of the order list.

line.description: The order, with its key and its values by name. describe_mission_name gives the value names.

before.description: The row of the order list that the order goes before, from 0. Without it, the order goes to the end.

add_order.description: Adds an order line to an order list, before a row or at the end. The key of the line is one of the 23 order keys, for example GotoVec.

prefab.description: The prefab: reference of a prefab of the active mod, for example prefab:mod:my_prefab.

id.description: The id of the new field. A line of the template names the field by this id.

label.description: The name of the field that the editor shows.

field_kind.description: The kind of the field: a value kind of the mission schema, list, triggers, condition or lines.

columns.description: The columns of a list field, each as 'id, kind, label'.

keys.description: The keys that a condition field or a lines field takes. Without them, the field takes each key.

tokens.description: The id of the word set of a field of the kind token.

unit.description: The unit of a number that the editor shows, for example s.

per_instance.description: True when each instance sets the value itself. Such a value never shows as an override.

optional.description: True when a value field can have no value. Each line with its slot then goes.

help.description: The help text of the field that the editor shows.

default.description: The default rows of the field in their text form.

index.description: The place of the field among the fields, from 0. Without it, the field goes to the end.

add_prefab_field.description: Adds a field to the template of a prefab of the active mod, in prefab mode. Each linked instance of the prefab compiles again.

script.description: The msn: reference of the script, or of its ship build file.

type.description: The section type, for example MsnSolar or NPCShipArch.

lines.description: The lines of the section, each with its key and its values by name.

before.description: The sec: reference of the section that the new section goes before. Without it, the section goes to the end.

add_section.description: Adds a section to a mission script or to its ship build file. A section with a nickname line gets a free name when its lines have none.

script.description: The msn: reference of the mission script.

nickname.description: The nickname of the new trigger. Without it, the editor makes a free name.

condition.description: The condition, for example {"key": "Cnd_Timer", "values": {"seconds": 3}}. Without it, the trigger has no condition.

actions.description: The action lines of the trigger, in order.

starts_with_mission.description: True writes InitState = ACTIVE, so the trigger starts with the mission.

repeats.description: True writes repeatable = true, so the trigger runs again when its condition is true again.

system.description: The system of the trigger, for example my_system. The editor shows it. The game does not read it.

x.description: The x of the point on the canvas of the mission graph.

y.description: The y of the point on the canvas of the mission graph.

place.description: The place of the node in the mission graph, in canvas points. Without it, the graph places the node.

act.description: The act: reference of the act that the trigger joins.

add_trigger.description: Adds a trigger at the end of a script. Without a nickname, the editor makes a free name.

order_list.description: The sec: reference of the order list.

position.description: The point: three numbers x, y and z.

before.description: The row of the order list that the line goes before, from 0. Without it, the line goes to the end.

add_waypoint.description: Adds a waypoint to an order list: a GotoVec line with the point. The other values of the line take their defaults.

script.description: The msn: reference of the mission script.

subject.description: The subject of the problem, for example M03|my_trigger|Cnd_True.

fix.description: The id of the fix, for example keepLast.

apply_fix.description: Runs a fix of a problem of the mission checks, as the fix button of the editor does. A fix that does not apply now refuses with FixNotFound.

instance.description: The inst: reference of the linked prefab instance.

field.description: The field of the override. Without field and member, each override of the instance goes to the prefab.

member.description: The role of a removed member. The prefab then removes the member too.

apply_override_to_prefab.description: Makes overrides of a linked instance the defaults of its prefab. Each linked instance of the prefab in the active mod compiles again. A built-in prefab and a prefab of a lower mod refuse.

ref.description: The line: reference of the line.

expect_key.description: The key that the line must have. Another key refuses with RowChanged.

expect_values.description: The value texts that the line must have. Other values refuse with RowChanged.

row.description: The line: an object with its line: reference in ref. The guards expect_key and expect_values are optional.

field.description: The id of the field of the prefab.

value.description: The name of the value in the line. Without it, the whole line is the slot.

bind_value.description: In prefab mode, makes a value of a line of the template the slot of a field. Without a value name, the whole line is the line of a condition field or a lines field.

commands.description: The commands of the group, in order.

expect_bodies.description: The guards of an inverse: the reference of each section and the hash of its lines. Another hash refuses with SectionChanged.

command_group.description: Runs commands in order as one step. The inverses use it. The budget of mission commands of a call counts each command in a group.

instance.description: The inst: reference of the linked prefab instance.

compile_prefab_instance.description: Compiles a linked instance again from its prefab and its fields. A hand edit of its lines goes, and the instance gets the changes of its prefab.

id.description: The id of the new prefab. The file of the prefab is prefabs\missions\<id>.ini.

name.description: The name in the library. Without it, the prefab takes the name of its source.

text.description: The whole text of the template. The inverse of a delete gives it.

variant_of.description: The prefab: reference of the prefab that the new prefab copies.

source.description: The inst: reference of the instance that becomes a linked instance of the new prefab.

fields.description: For a linked source: the fields whose overrides become the defaults. Without it, each override becomes a default.

create_prefab_asset.description: Makes a prefab of the active mod. The start is a template text, another prefab for a variant, or an instance. A source instance becomes a linked instance of the new prefab.

path.description: The install path of the new script in a folder under DATA\MISSIONS outside the encounters folder, for example DATA\MISSIONS\MY\my_mission.ini.

ship_build_file.description: The install path of the ship build file, for example DATA\MISSIONS\MY\npcships.ini. A file that does not exist becomes a new file.

type.description: The section type, for example MsnShip.

key.description: The key of the line.

values.description: The value texts of the line by position.

entries.description: The lines of the section in order, each with its key and its value texts.

sections.description: The sections of the script. Without them, the script has one [Mission] section. The inverse of a delete gives them.

ship_build_sections.description: The sections of a new ship build file. The inverse of a delete gives them.

create_script.description: Makes a new mission script: a whole file of the active mod under DATA\MISSIONS with one [Mission] section. With a ship build file, the [Mission] section names it.

script.description: The msn: reference of the script, or of the ship build file.

delete_script.description: Deletes a whole mission file of the active mod: a script, or the ship build file of a script. A file of the game data or of a lower mod cannot go. The ship build file of a script goes too when no other script names it.

item.description: The sec: reference of the item.

new_name.description: The nickname of the copy. Without it, the editor makes a free name.

duplicate_item.description: Copies an item with a new nickname to the end of its file. The lines that name the original do not change.

trigger.description: The trg: reference of the trigger.

new_name.description: The nickname of the copy. Without it, the editor makes a free name.

x.description: The x of the point on the canvas of the mission graph.

y.description: The y of the point on the canvas of the mission graph.

place.description: The place of the node of the copy in the mission graph, in canvas points. Without it, the graph places the node.

duplicate_trigger.description: Copies a trigger to the end of the script with a new nickname. A line of the copy that names the original names the copy.

section.description: The sec: reference of the section, or the trg: reference of a trigger.

line.description: The new line: an object with its key and its values by name. Or give its value texts by position in texts.

before.description: The row that the line goes before, from 0. Without it, the line goes to the end.

insert_line.description: Inserts any line into a section of a mission file, before a row or at the end. A second nickname line is not allowed.

ref.description: The line: reference of the line.

expect_key.description: The key that the line must have. Another key refuses with RowChanged.

expect_values.description: The value texts that the line must have. Other values refuse with RowChanged.

row.description: The Act_ActTrig line of the link: an object with its line: reference in ref.

condition.description: The condition of the new trigger, with its key and its values by name.

nickname.description: The nickname of the new trigger. Without it, the editor makes a free name.

x.description: The x of the point on the canvas of the mission graph.

y.description: The y of the point on the canvas of the mission graph.

place.description: The place of the node in the mission graph, in canvas points. Without it, the graph places the node.

insert_trigger_on_link.description: Puts a new trigger on a Start link. The new trigger has the condition and starts the old target. The line of the link then starts the new trigger.

source.description: The trg: reference of the trigger that gets the action lines.

target.description: The nickname of the target trigger in the same script. A name that does not resolve adds the error M05.

link_kind.description: The kind of the link: start, stop or restart.

before.description: The row of the source that the lines go before, from 0. Without it, the lines go to the end.

link_triggers.description: Links two triggers. start writes Act_ActTrig, stop writes Act_DeactTrig, and restart writes Act_DeactTrig and then Act_ActTrig.

ref.description: The line: reference of the line.

expect_key.description: The key that the line must have. Another key refuses with RowChanged.

expect_values.description: The value texts that the line must have. Other values refuse with RowChanged.

row.description: The line: an object with its line: reference in ref. The guards expect_key and expect_values are optional.

before.description: The row before the move that the line goes before, from 0. Without it, the line goes to the end.

move_line.description: Moves any line of a section before another row, or to the end. The first nickname line cannot move.

script.description: The msn: reference of the mission script.

trigger.description: The nickname of the trigger.

x.description: The x of the node on the canvas of the mission graph.

y.description: The y of the node on the canvas of the mission graph.

remove.description: True removes the place, so the graph places the node again.

index.description: The place of a new record in the list of the node records, from 0. The inverses use it.

places.description: The new place of each node.

move_nodes.description: Sets the places of trigger nodes in the graph file of a script. The game does not read the graph file.

section.description: The sec: reference of the ship or of the formation.

before.description: The sec: reference of the section that the section goes before. Without it, the section goes to the end.

move_section.description: Moves a ship or a formation section before another section of its file, or to the end. The place of another section type has no effect in the game.

ship.description: The sec: reference of the mission ship.

position.description: The position: three numbers x, y and z.

rotation.description: The orientation: four numbers, as an orientation line holds them.

system.description: The nickname of the system of the ship, for example my_system.

anchor.description: The nickname of the object, for example my_station.

heading.description: The heading from the object, in degrees.

range.description: The range from the object, in meters. It is optional.

near.description: A place near an object, in place of the position. The command writes a rel_pos line.

place_mission_ship.description: Places a mission ship: its position, orientation and system lines, or its rel_pos line near an object.

script.description: The msn: reference of the mission script.

prefab.description: The prefab: reference of the prefab, for example prefab:builtin:spawnWave or prefab:mod:my_prefab.

id.description: The id of the instance. Without it, the editor makes an id.

field.description: The id of the field.

rows.description: The rows of the value in their text form.

values.description: The value of each field. A field without a value takes the default of the prefab.

trigger.description: The nickname of the outside trigger that the port starts.

ports.description: The outside trigger that each port starts.

removed.description: The roles of the members that the new instance does not have.

x.description: The x of the point on the canvas of the mission graph.

y.description: The y of the point on the canvas of the mission graph.

place.description: The place of the first member trigger in the mission graph. Without it, the graph places the nodes.

act.description: The act: reference of the act that the member triggers join.

place_prefab_instance.description: Places a linked instance of a prefab in a script. The compiled sections go to the end of the script, and the record goes into the graph file.

act.description: The act: reference of the act.

remove_act.description: Removes an act from the graph file. Its triggers stay. When no act stays, the graph shows the acts that it proposes.

ref.description: The line: reference of the line.

expect_key.description: The key that the line must have. Another key refuses with RowChanged.

expect_values.description: The value texts that the line must have. Other values refuse with RowChanged.

row.description: The action line: an object with its line: reference in ref.

remove_action.description: Removes an action line of a trigger.

item.description: The sec: reference of the item.

remove_item.description: Removes an item of a mission file. The lines that name it stay and show 'Missing'. An [NPC] that a ship names refuses, and so does a ship build that an [NPC] names.

item.description: The sec: reference of the item.

line.description: A line: its key, and its values by name. A key can be in more than one section type, so each definition of a key fits.

inverse.description: The mission command that reverts the mission commands of the call. Give it to mission_edit after later edits. It refuses when a later edit changed one of its sections.

trigger.description: The trg: reference of the trigger of the line.

from.description: The index of the line in the trigger before the call, from 0.

to.description: The index of the line in the trigger after the call, from 0.

row_moves.description: The lines of triggers whose place in their trigger changed. Each line comes once, with its place before the call and its place after the call.

status.description: applied: the data changed in one Undo step. no_change: nothing changed. previewed: a preview that changed nothing.

code.description: The kind of the error. Each kind has a fixed meaning, for example not_found or invalid_argument.

detail.description: The detail code of the error, for example ReferenceNotFound or BadArgument.

message.description: What is wrong and how to correct it.

index.description: The index of the step of a batch that failed, or none.

target.description: The reference or the text that the error is about, or none.

field.description: The argument or the field that the error is about, or none.

step_code.description: For the error step_failed: the code of the error of the step, for example not_found. Else none.

errors.description: The errors of a refusal. A tool error gives them as the error of the call.

label.description: The label of the edit, for example Delete my_station_1.

undo_label.description: The label of the Undo step, for example Agent: Delete my_station_1, or none without a step.

rev.description: The revision of the edit view after the call, as text. A preview and a call without a change keep it.

versions.description: The versions of the mission scripts that the edit changed, by install path.

files.description: The install paths of the files that the edit changed.

adds.description: The references of the new items.

changes.description: The references of the items that the edit changed and kept.

ref.description: The reference of the removed item.

why.description: target for an item of the request, cascade for an item that goes with a target.

cause.description: For a cascade: the line that names the target. Else none.

deletes.description: The items that the edit removed.

renames.description: The items that got a new name, with the old and the new reference.

ref.description: The reference of the section of the lines.

key.description: The key of the first line.

fixes.description: The lines that the edit changed because they name an item that the edit removed.

tools.description: When the active mod has unsaved edits, the editor asks the user to save them first. When the user turned on the automatic save for an agent Play, the editor saves without a question. Then the tool starts the game in OpenLancer at a point in space or at a base. base.description: The base of a start at a base: its nickname or its base: reference, for example my_base_01.

play.description: The state of Play in OpenLancer when the request ended: idle, starting, validating, running, reloading, not_responding or stopping.

tools.name: render_scene
tools.title: Render an image of a system
tools.description: Renders an image of a system from a camera. The tool does not move the camera of the user and does not open the system in the Scene. Only the editor host can render. Y is up. The result gives the place of each item in the image.

system.description: The system of the image: its nickname or its system: reference. The default is the system that the Scene shows.

position.description: The position of the camera in meters: X, Y and Z. Y is up.

look_at.description: The point that the camera looks at, in meters: X, Y and Z.

fov.description: The horizontal angle of the whole image in degrees. The default is the angle of the Scene camera.

camera.description: The camera of the image. Without it, the camera frames the items of frame, or the whole system. A view straight down has -Z at the top of the image.

frame.description: The references of the items to show, for example obj:my_station_1. Each item must be in the system of the image. The camera looks at them from above and from the front, as the Scene frames an item.

width.description: The width of the image in pixels. studio_status gives the largest value.

height.description: The height of the image in pixels. studio_status gives the largest value.

zones.description: Show the volumes of the zones, nebulae and asteroid fields, and the patrol paths. The visible items then also include the zones.

system.description: The system: reference of the image.

width.description: The width of the image in pixels.

height.description: The height of the image in pixels.

position.description: The position of the camera in meters: X, Y and Z.

look_at.description: The point that the camera looks at, in meters: X, Y and Z.

fov.description: The horizontal angle of the whole image in degrees.

camera.description: The camera of the image. Give it to render_scene again for the same view.

zones.description: True when the image shows the zone volumes and the patrol paths.

ref.description: The reference of the item: obj: or zone:.

x.description: The distance of the center of the item from the left edge of the image, in pixels.

y.description: The distance of the center of the item from the top edge of the image, in pixels.

radius.description: The radius of the item in the image, in pixels.

distance.description: The distance of the item from the camera along the view direction, in meters.

visible.description: The items whose bounding spheres are in the view, the largest first, with their places in pixels. Another item can hide an item of the list. An item whose center is behind the camera is not in the list.

visible_total.description: The number of all items in the view. The list can have fewer rows.
